about: Rules for Glowie (skincare assistant). General, cosmetic-level guidance only — not medical advice. Edit freely: the app reads this file every time.

oily.label: Oily
oily.description: Shiny all over a few hours after washing; pores may look larger.

morning.why: Removes overnight oil without stripping the skin.
Oily skin still needs water-based hydration; dehydrated skin can make more oil.
Protects against sun damage without feeling greasy.

night.why: Removes sunscreen, oil and dirt from the day.

avoid: Heavy oils and thick butters (e.g. coconut oil, cocoa butter) on the face
Harsh alcohol-based toners that over-dry and can trigger more oil

dry.label: Dry
dry.description: Feels tight, rough or flaky, especially after washing.

morning.product: Creamy, non-foaming cleanser (or just lukewarm water)
morning.why: Cleans without removing the skin's natural oils.

morning.product: Rich moisturiser with ceramides and glycerin
morning.why: Repairs the skin barrier and locks in water.
Protects against sun damage; creams add extra moisture.

night.product: Hyaluronic acid serum on damp skin

avoid: Foaming cleansers with SLS (sodium lauryl sulfate)
Very hot water and long hot showers

normal.label: Normal
normal.description: Comfortable most of the day — not very shiny, not tight.

morning.why: Keeps skin clean without upsetting its balance.
The most important anti-ageing and anti-spot step.

combination.label: Combination
combination.description: Oily on the forehead, nose and chin (T-zone) but normal or dry on the cheeks.

morning.why: Controls T-zone oil without drying the cheeks.

morning.product: Light gel-cream moisturiser (a little extra on dry areas)

morning.why: Lightweight sun protection for the whole face.

night.why: Removes the day's oil and sunscreen.

night.product: Light gel-cream moisturiser (richer cream only on dry patches)
night.why: Gives each area what it needs.

acne.label: Acne / breakouts

night.why: Gets inside pores and helps unclog them.
night.start: Start 2–3 nights a week, then increase if your skin is comfortable.

tips: Change pillowcases 1–2 times a week and keep phone screens clean.
Look for products labelled "non-comedogenic".
Give acne products 6–8 weeks before judging results.

dark_spots.label: Dark spots / uneven tone

morning.why: Brightens and helps fade dark spots; also boosts sun protection.

night.start: Every night, or alternate nights at first.

avoid: Skipping sunscreen — the sun makes dark spots darker
Unlabelled "skin-whitening" creams (some contain harmful mercury or steroids)
tips: Daily sunscreen is the single most important step for dark spots.
Spots usually fade slowly — expect 2–3 months.

wrinkles.label: Fine lines / wrinkles

night.why: Encourages skin renewal and smoother texture.
night.start: Start 2 nights a week; build up slowly over a month.

avoid: Using retinol and strong exfoliating acids on the same night
Applying retinol on damp skin (it stings more)
tips: Retinol makes skin more sun-sensitive — sunscreen every morning is a must.
Mild dryness or flaking in the first weeks is common; use more moisturiser.

dark_circles.label: Dark circles

morning.product: Eye cream with caffeine or niacinamide
morning.why: May make under-eye darkness and puffiness look less obvious.
morning.start: Pat gently with your ring finger.

tips: Dark circles are often genetic or caused by thin skin and shadows — creams help only a little.
Regular sleep and staying hydrated help; a colour-correcting concealer gives instant results.

redness.label: Redness / easily irritated

morning.product: Soothing serum with centella asiatica or panthenol

night.product: Soothing serum with centella asiatica or panthenol

tips: Redness that lasts, burns or keeps coming back should be checked by a doctor.

dullness.label: Dullness

morning.why: Adds brightness and protects from pollution.

night.why: Gently removes dead skin cells for a smoother glow.
night.start: Never on the same night as retinol.

avoid: Exfoliating more than 2–3 times a week
tips: Sleep, water and daily sunscreen make a visible difference.

large_pores.label: Large-looking pores

morning.why: Helps control oil so pores look smaller.

tips: Pore size is mostly genetic — products can make pores look smaller, not remove them.

sensitive.label: Sensitive skin
tips: Patch test every new product on your inner arm or behind the ear for 24–48 hours first.
Add only one new product every 2 weeks.
Use the lowest strength of any active ingredient and start 2 nights a week.

pregnant.label: Pregnant or breastfeeding

retinoid.why: A gentler option often chosen during pregnancy instead of retinol.

tips: Retinoids (retinol, tretinoin, adapalene) are usually avoided during pregnancy and breastfeeding.
Please check every skincare product with your doctor or midwife.

under_18.label: Under 18

retinoid.why: A gentle, teen-friendly way to support smoother-looking skin.

tips: Keep it simple: a gentle cleanser, moisturiser and sunscreen are enough for most teenage skin.
Hormones often cause breakouts at this age — be gentle and see a doctor if acne is painful or leaves marks.
Retinol and strong acids aren't needed at this age unless a doctor recommends them.
This is the best time to build habits: daily sunscreen now prevents most dark spots and early lines later.
Skin renewal starts to slow from the mid-20s — an antioxidant like vitamin C in the morning helps protect it.
If you'd like to start retinol for prevention, begin with a low strength (0.2–0.3%) twice a week.

night.why: Supports skin renewal and firmness, which slow down with age.
night.start: Start 2 nights a week; build up slowly over a month.

tips: Skin often gets a little drier after 35 — choose a slightly richer moisturiser if it feels tight.
Remember your neck and the backs of your hands when applying sunscreen.

45_plus.label: 45 and above

night.start: Start 2 nights a week; build up slowly over a month.

tips: Skin makes less oil with age — a richer, ceramide-based moisturiser at night helps a lot.
Hormonal changes (such as menopause) can make skin drier and more sensitive; patch test new products.
Get a yearly skin check for any spots or moles that change.

light: Lighter skin burns more easily — reapply sunscreen every 2 hours when outdoors.
medium: Medium skin can get dark marks after spots or sun — daily sunscreen helps keep tone even.
tan: Tan skin is prone to dark marks after breakouts — treat spots early and don't pick them.
If a mineral sunscreen looks grey or white, try a tinted or chemical-filter SPF.
deep: Mineral sunscreens can leave a white cast on deep skin — tinted or chemical-filter SPF usually blends better.
Deeper skin tones are more prone to dark marks after spots or irritation, so choose gentle actives and avoid picking.

dermatologist.cystic_acne: You mentioned deep, painful lumps. These can leave scars and usually need prescription treatment — please see a dermatologist.
dermatologist.many_acne: If breakouts cover large areas or don't improve after 2–3 months of a consistent routine, please see a dermatologist.
dermatologist.changing_spot: You mentioned a spot or mole that is changing, bleeding or itching. Please get it checked by a doctor soon — this app can't assess it.
dermatologist.persistent_redness: Redness that lasts for weeks, burns or keeps returning is worth showing to a doctor.

general_tips: Use sunscreen every morning — even indoors near windows and on cloudy days.
Introduce new products one at a time so you can tell what works (or what irritates).
Give a routine 6–8 weeks before judging the results.
